specification.family_title: Commit outcome after a connection or reply failure
specification.title: COMMIT completes on the server, and the client discards the reply (client-side simulation)
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API.
Arm the client-side fault: the driver sends the next COMMIT, which PostgreSQL executes; the driver then closes its own connection and reports a connection error instead of the reply.
End the transaction normally, so that the framework sends COMMIT.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: When the connection or PostgreSQL's reply was lost around COMMIT, so that the client never received an acknowledgement of COMMIT, the API does not report a successful commit.
When COMMIT may have reached PostgreSQL and no reply arrived, the API does not report a confirmed rollback, through its result, its errors, or its rollback hooks or events.

execution.description: sql.DB.BeginTx, sql.Tx.Commit, and sql.Tx.Rollback. sql.TxOptions.Isolation is set for TX-05. A nil Commit error is reported as committed. pgx.ErrTxCommitRollback is reported as rolled_back. Any other Commit or Rollback error is reported as failed. The pool is database/sql, not pgxpool. stdlib ResetSession still returns driver.ErrBadConn when the pgx transaction status is not idle.

configuration.nested: SAVEPOINT / ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT / RELEASE SAVEPOINT as SQL. database/sql has no savepoint type.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A client-side simulation inside the adapter's driver layer (node-postgres, pg.Client.prototype.query): COMMIT is sent and completes on the server; the client then closes its own connection, and the caller receives a connection error instead of the reply. It is not a network failure. Artifact: the driver has already parsed PostgreSQL's reply (its transaction status reads idle) before the simulated loss, where a real loss leaves it reading in-transaction. The case therefore establishes only whether the API claims an outcome after its COMMIT call fails, not behaviour that depends on the driver's state, such as pool recovery.
fault.injection_point: In the client, between the server's reply to COMMIT and its delivery to the framework.
fault.preconditions: The framework's statements pass through the instrumented pg module (recorded as trace_sees_framework_pg).
fault.expected_client: A connection error in place of the reply to COMMIT.

knowledge: None at the API level: the reply to COMMIT was discarded before the framework saw it. Only a later read can establish that the transaction committed.

api_outcome.basis: sql.Tx.Commit returned an error that does not assert a rollback
api_outcome.contract: Go database/sql Tx.Commit returns the error from driver.Tx.Commit and does not add a command tag (database/sql/sql.go). pgx stdlib v5.11.0 wrapTx.Commit calls pgx.Tx.Commit and returns that error (stdlib/sql.go). A nil error is database/sql's report that the transaction committed. pgx.ErrTxCommitRollback therefore reaches the caller as a non-nil error. stdlib Conn.ResetSession returns driver.ErrBadConn when pgx's transaction status is not idle, so the pool discards that connection before the next checkout. database/sql has no savepoint type. This control sends SAVEPOINT, ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT, and RELEASE SAVEPOINT as SQL.
